questions.stem: How does Data Enrichment relate to Self-Service?
options: Data Enrichment is a synonym for Self-Service
Data Enrichment must be completed before any Self-Service is possible
Data Enrichment is just one part of one of the types of Self-Service
Data Enrichment replaces Self-Service in the analytics era
Data Enrichment and Self-Service are unrelated
questions.explanation: Self-Service and Data Enrichment are often confused, but Data Enrichment is just one part of one of the types of Self-Service.

options: Empowering business users and decision makers to conduct activities themselves to shorten end-to-end delivery time
Transferring all reporting work to the IT department
Allowing customers to update their own bank balances
Automating the hiring of data scientists
Replacing business users with machine learning
questions.explanation: Self-Service empowers business users and decision makers to conduct activities by themselves in order to shorten the end-to-end delivery time.

questions.stem: What does I Am Datapedia! say is a prerequisite for any type of Self-Service?
questions.explanation: Because it is risky to let people change things they do not understand, Data Democratisation is a prerequisite for any type of Self-Service.

questions.stem: Why is Self-Service described as risky without the right foundation?
options: Because it allows people to make changes when they do not understand the data
Because it slows down delivery time
Because it removes access control from systems
Because it can only be used by IT
questions.explanation: It is too risky to allow people to go and make changes if they do not understand data, which is why Data Democratisation must come first.

questions.stem: Which capabilities belong to Data Self-Service?
options: Running deep learning models on unstructured data
A data-friendly environment where users are trained on data, may question its accuracy and integrity, and may extend its context through Data Enrichment
questions.explanation: In Data Self-Service a data-friendly environment is provided, users are trained, allowed to question accuracy and integrity, and allowed to enrich first-hand data with second-hand and third-party datasets.

questions.stem: Who are the major users of Analytics Self-Service, and what do they do?
options: Data Citizens, who run data science or data mining models using low-code or no-code tools
External auditors, who verify financial statements
questions.explanation: Analytics Self-Service involves machine learning and data modelling; Data Citizens are its major users, running data science or data mining models with low-code or no-code tools.

questions.stem: What does BI Self-Service allow users to do?
options: Connect to internal or external source systems, within their access level, and create their own reports and dashboards
questions.explanation: In BI Self-Service, users connect to any internal or external source system, based on their access level, and create reports and dashboards on their own.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of BI Self-Service?
options: To increase the number of data scientists
To eliminate the need for access control
To reduce the dependency on IT for creating reports for business users
questions.explanation: BI Self-Service exists majorly to reduce the dependency on IT to create reports for business users.

questions.stem: In the current era, how has the paradigm of report and dashboard creation shifted?
questions.explanation: The paradigm of creating reports and dashboards has moved from IT to business users.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the types of Self-Service discussed in I Am Datapedia!?
questions.explanation: The three types discussed are Data Self-Service, Analytics Self-Service (for Data Citizens) and BI Self-Service; Infrastructure Self-Service is not among them.
